newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk protest won't hit output - independent union.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk protest won't hit output - independent union.

text.p: The head of Russia's Federation of Independent Trade Unions, Mikhail Shmakov, said on Wednesday that the main plant of Norilsk Nickel would take part in nationwide protests on March 27 but that it would not stop output.

"The Norilsk Nickel combine will participate in the action, but it will not stop production," Shmakov told a news conference. But he said that other Norilsk subsidiaries would take part in the protest.
The Federation represents a broad, large group of trade unions across Russia.
He did not comment upon fuller Norilsk action planned for April 2.
Workers at the main Norilsk plant, the mining and metallurgical combine, have threatened to disrupt output on March 27 and from April 2 over salary and holiday arrears and related issues.
The plant is a subsidiary of RAO Norilsky Nickel NKEL.RTS 0#NKEL.RUO, a major world producer of nickel, platinum group metals and other metals.
